newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Spectacular launch for VSNL boosts GDRs.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Spectacular launch for VSNL boosts GDRs.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts edged higher after a moderate trading day, with most attention focused on the successful launch of a debut GDR for Indian telecom firm VSNL.
"It's been a spectacular debut," said one trader here. "It was issued at $13.93 and it ended at $16.50 -- it has boosted the tone for GDRs."
Another trader said the VSNL launch, previously twice delayed, plus the recent market-friendly budget, had given the entire market a sentiment boost.
Indian GDRs rose 2.54 points of 3.40 percent to 77.39 on the HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI, with the premium over the local market at 19.22 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index was closed for a market holiday but ended last week at 3,730.20.

Korean GDRs held up despite local market weakness based on fears of economic fallout from a renewed probe into a loans scandal. But some London GDR traders reported strength, particularly in banking GDRs.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 1.67 points or 3.09 percent stronger at 55.79, a premium of 37.29 percent over the local market.
The Korea Composite Index ended 5.87 points or 0.94 percent lower at 617.26.
Taiwan GDRs had a quiet trading day amid feares of renewed friction with China.
"The market's been spooked by the Chinese news," said one trader, but added most players were willing to sit out the latest round of jitters.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended 1.76 points or 1.57 percent weaker at 109.91, a negative premium of 0.31 percent.
The Taiwan Weighted Index plunged 3.49 percent to 7,946.88.
